ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Missouri Amendment 3: Repeal 2024 abortion-rights amendment; abortion limits; gender transition procedures for minors
ballotMeasures.summary:
Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: Repeal the 2024 voter-approved Amendment providing reproductive healthcare rights, including abortion through fetal viability; Allow abortions for rape and incest (under twelve-weeks’ gestation), emergencies, and fetal anomalies; Allow legislation regulating abortion; Ensure parental consent for minors’ abortions; Prohibit gender transition procedures for minors?

In short: Legislatively referred amendment that would repeal the 2024 reproductive-freedom amendment, allow abortion only for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, and rape or incest before twelve weeks, and prohibit gender transition procedures for minors.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.sos.mo.gov/petitions/2026ballotmeasures

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Missouri Amendment 6: Initiative and referendum powers; limits on legislative changes to voter-passed measures
ballotMeasures.summary:
Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: expand the initiative and referendum petition process by making it a fundamental right; allow courts to revise ballot summaries through lawsuits; prohibit the legislature from weakening initiative or referendum powers; prohibit the legislature from changing or repealing laws enacted through the initiative process, or passing laws similar to those rejected by referendum, without approval from at least 80% of both chambers; and preserve existing majority vote and signature requirements for initiative and referendum petitions?

In short: Citizen-initiated amendment that would make initiative and referendum a fundamental right and bar the legislature from changing or repealing voter-enacted measures unless at least 80% of each chamber refers the change to voters.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.sos.mo.gov/petitions/2026ballotmeasures

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Missouri Amendment 7: Show-Me Prosperity Fund endowment to replace state taxes
ballotMeasures.summary:
Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to establish a permanent public endowment fund to support state government instead of taxing Missouri residents, prohibit the General Assembly from appropriating or diverting the fund, and eliminate state-imposed taxes once the fund generates sufficient revenue to replace them?

In short: Legislatively referred amendment that would create a permanent state investment fund whose earnings, once sufficient as certified by the State Treasurer, would replace and eliminate state-imposed taxes.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.sos.mo.gov/petitions/2026ballotmeasures

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Missouri Amendment 8: Election and removal of county sheriffs
ballotMeasures.summary:
Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to support law enforcement by preserving the right of citizens to elect a county sheriff, prohibiting the removal of a county sheriff except by a writ of quo warranto, and recognizing the office of sheriff as part of the administration of justice?

In short: Legislatively referred amendment that would put the election of county sheriffs in the constitution and allow removal of a sheriff only through a quo warranto action brought by the Attorney General.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.sos.mo.gov/petitions/2026ballotmeasures

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Missouri Proposition A: Referendum on the 2025 congressional district map (House Bill 1)
ballotMeasures.summary:
Do the people of the state of Missouri approve the act of the General Assembly entitled “House Bill No. 1 (2025 Second Extraordinary Session),” which repeals Missouri’s existing congressional plan, and replaces it with new congressional boundaries that keep more counties intact?

In short: Citizen veto referendum on the congressional map passed in 2025: a yes vote approves the new districts, a no vote keeps the districts enacted in 2022.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.sos.mo.gov/petitions/2026ballotmeasures
